gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $1,305 Solis S6-EH1P5K-H-US '5 kW hybrid' only accepts a 120–500 V high-voltage lithium battery, so it cannot use the 48 V battery banks that the Sol-Ark 5K and Rich Solar NOVA 3K on the same answer are built around; the five '3–5 kW' cards are not comparable on battery voltage, output voltage or backup capability.
standout_why: I compared against liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters (rank 1) and offgridbenchmark.com/inverters/best/off-grid (rank 7), and I read ChatGPT's answer text. liveoffthegrid has continuous, surge, battery-voltage and output-voltage columns, but it does not include the Solis S6, SMA Sunny Boy, Sol-Ark 5K or Rich Solar NOVA 3K. It gives surge figures without a duration and says nothing about grid export. offgridbenchmark leaves the battery voltage, PV input and output voltage rows empty, and it also lacks the Solis, SMA, Sol-Ark 5K and Rich Solar. ChatGPT's own cards label the Sol-Ark and Rich Solar '48V' but give no battery voltage for the Solis. None of them says the Solis needs a 120–500 V battery. None of them says the Sunny Boy has no battery input and is end-of-life. None of them says the $2,998 Sol-Ark 5K split-phase listing is off-grid only in California and Hawaii. gearranking.com could not be read because of a certificate error.
decides: This changes the pick. The cheapest '5 kW hybrid' (Solis, $1,305) is only cheap before the battery: it needs a 120–500 V high-voltage pack, not a common 48 V LiFePO4 rack like the Sun Gold Power SG48100P that Dealectric lists. A shopper who already has or wants 48 V batteries should be steered to a 48 V hybrid: the Sol-Ark 5K, or the NOVA 3K for 120 V-only off-grid use. The SMA Sunny Boy 5.0 should not be in a 'hybrid/backup' comparison at all, because it lists no battery input and its retailer marks it discontinued. The Renogy 3000W has no PV input, so it is not a solar inverter on its own. Californian and Hawaiian shoppers should know RENVU says the $2,998 Sol-Ark 5K split-phase is off-grid only in those markets, and RENVU's cheaper $1,486 Sol-Ark 5K is described as 'perfect for 120V only setups'.
